gap.summary: R1 scaffold proved the runtime can exist as a repository-native scaffold, but two runtime gaps remained: B1-B6 anti-overstep bindings were loaded but not behaviorally used (decorative registry), and run() could mutate caller-owned source/observation lifecycle fields. R2 closes both and proves the scaffold over 48 genuine heterogeneous real objects without state pollution, hidden second executor, false causal promotion, false consensus or privacy leakage.
evidence: R1 evidence doc records NB-1 (bindings param unused) and NB-2 (run() mutates caller input in place) as known limitations.
R2 commit 2 replaces the hardcoded _apply_anti_overstep with a fail-closed registry interpreter and deep-copies caller inputs at run() entry.
gap.smallest_material_action: R2 commit 2 edits tools/adaptive_relational_runtime/runtime.py to replace the hardcoded _apply_anti_overstep branch with a registry interpreter and to deep-copy caller source/observation at run() entry; no new capability or executor is introduced.

claim_ceiling: candidate_repository_pilot_capability_only: ARR R2 pilot closes the R1 registry-behavior and caller-input-mutation gaps and runs 48 real objects under a strict privacy boundary. It does not add a truth layer, L7, execution engine, external action, auto-PROMOTE/EVOLVE or causal upgrade, and is not the full 836-note corpus run.
